(1) local features for non-planar scenes can be viewpoint invariant; (2) viewpoint invariant features necessarily sacrifice shape information; (3) if viewpoint is factore d out in the matching process, then shape information can be recovered.

(a) viewpoint invariant features are possible for non planar scenes; (b) they sacrifice shape information in the representation; (c) they can be used in a matching scheme that is viewpoint invariant, and shape discriminative; and (d) this matching scheme can improve matching performance even in planar scenes.

(i) local features can be viewpoint invariant for generic scenes; (ii) this invariance necessarily comes at a cost of shape discriminability; and (iii) shape discriminability can be recovered by factoring viewpoint out during matching.
